During a severe storm at Kestrel Ridge Observatory that closed the single access road, a grid power outage began at 00:58. The standby generator started automatically about twenty seconds later and ran for 38 minutes before shutting down at 01:36. While night operator Imre Soller was on duty in the control room and visiting astronomer Dr. Odalys Renk was in the visitor wing, the generator stoppage caused the control room lighting to fail and the dome drive to stop, though battery-backed computers remained on while the uninterruptible power supply was available. Staff cottage resident and site engineer Talwen Pryce walked through the snow in about ten minutes to respond, accessing the generator panel to reset the lockout state and successfully restart the unit at 02:04. Fuel tank level records confirmed steady readings of 61 percent at 01:00 and 48 percent at 02:00, with no sudden drops recorded. However, conflicting accounts remain regarding the exact cause of the generator trip, with log data and engineering assessment pointing to overheating protection triggered by snow-blocked cooling air intakes, contrasted with operator observations suggesting a low oil pressure trip.

An operations review of the incident at the Veltrane Dye Depot on the Orsel Canal wharf shows that a fire started in the cold-storage annex shortly after 04:00 on 22 October. The annex smoke detector panel recorded an alarm on zone 2 at 04:06, and backup battery power engaged at 04:17 following a mains power failure. Security cameras captured the annex roller door glowing orange at 04:09 before power was lost at 04:31. A passing canal barge pilot made the initial emergency call at 04:12, reporting flames visible through the upper vents. The first pumper departed the station at 04:14, growing to five appliances at the peak of the response. Firefighters utilized a floating suction hose to draw water from the canal, and the wharf road remained closed until mid-morning. One firefighter sustained a minor wrist burn and returned to duty. The sole supervisor observed normal compressor function during a 03:30 walk-round and safely evacuated six warehouse staff through the loading door, accounting for all personnel in the yard within minutes. The loss adjuster estimated a total roof collapse of the annex, which contained approximately forty pallets of powdered pigment and refrigerated dye concentrate, while the main warehouse suffered only smoke and water damage.

Sources: Night supervisor Imre Dallow, Orsel Wharf Fire Brigade incident log, Canalside Logistics security camera system, Insurance loss adjuster Teodor Quill, Annex smoke detector panel, Dispatcher Pira Voss's call record

Shortly after four in the morning on October twenty-second, a fire broke out in the cold-storage annex of the Veltrane Dye Depot located on the Orsel Canal wharf, which held about forty pallets of powdered pigment and refrigerated dye concentrate. The annex smoke detector panel recorded an initial alarm on zone two, and security cameras showed the annex roller door glowing orange at four-nine. A passing canal barge pilot made the first emergency call at four-twelve, reporting flames visible through the upper vents. The first pumper left the station at four-fourteen, and emergency appliances arrived at the scene. Mains power to the annex failed at four-seventeen, prompting the detector panel to switch to its backup battery, while cameras on the north wharf lost power at four-thirty-one. Night supervisor Imre Dallow, the only supervisor on site, noted that refrigeration compressors had been running normally during his three-thirty walk-round. Following the outbreak, Dallow led six warehouse staff out through the loading door, and a headcount in the yard confirmed everyone was accounted for within minutes. Firefighters drew water from the Orsel Canal using a floating suction hose, and the wharf road was closed to traffic until mid-morning. One firefighter was treated at the scene for a minor wrist burn and returned to duty. The annex roof collapsed entirely, while the main warehouse suffered only smoke and water damage.

An incident occurred on a Thursday in May when the freight elevator in the Finishing Building of the Lindqvist Textile Mill stopped between the second and third floors while moving upward. Finishing floor supervisor Imogen Pask went to the third-floor landing to communicate with Bram through the closed doors and subsequently arranged to transport the remaining fabric bolts to the third floor using the stairs and a small passenger lift. Elevator technician Dorrel Vance arrived and signed in at the gate at 1:48 p.m., then went directly to the roof machine room to isolate the main power supply.
